pattern_tile_puzzle.name: Pattern Tile Puzzle
pattern_tile_puzzle.description: Create patterns on a small tile grid. Watch them repeat across a carpet. Handmade meets computational - from textile traditions to pixel art.
pattern_tile_puzzle.qfep_connection: Pattern-making as play: paint a small tile, watch it repeat across a carpet, adjust, repeat. Handmade meets computational — the room where the abstract truth (a pattern is a tiled array) becomes a thing your hands discover by doing, the carpet answering every edit instantly.

dna.default: motif=blank, dyelot=natural - _motif_value() returns 0 for every cell, which is literally the old `row.append(0)`, and DYELOTS has no `natural` key so _apply_dyelot() returns before touching the palette literal. The 33 existing placements render byte for byte as before. Their tokens carry config (#p4m, #cursor, :270) so apply_grid_config DOES run for them, but neither key is present, so the has()+differs guard never fires a rebuild.
dna.was: an empty grid over an empty carpet in one fixed set of eight yarns - the artifact argued that a small decision is amplified by a symmetry rule, and then shipped with no decision made and one dye range to make it in, so every photograph of it showed the amplifier with nothing in it
dna.note: Both axes live on the SHARED script behind six registry tokens (pattern_tile_puzzle, _4x4, _mirror, _8x8, _brick, _herringbone), which differ only by config {tile_size, repeat_mode}. They are declared HERE, on the 33-placement member, and the siblings inherit the knobs, set neither, and keep their appearance. motif is written as a function of (x, y, tile_size) so it holds at the family's 4 and 8 alike. NOT promoted: repeat_mode / wallpaper_group - real, and the artifact's own critical_parameter, but they are already how this family spells its members apart, so sweeping them would measure the siblings rather than a variation within one.

pattern_tile_4x4.name: 4x4 Pattern Tile
pattern_tile_4x4.description: Basic 4x4 tile pattern editor. Simple repeat mode.
pattern_tile_4x4.qfep_connection: The atom of pattern: a 4×4 grid you paint, set to repeat. The smallest complete lesson in the chapter — a tile is a tiny 2D array, and tiling is that array copied across the plane, so a whole carpet is one small list of cells, addressed modulo its size.

pattern_tile_mirror.name: Mirror Pattern Tile
pattern_tile_mirror.qfep_connection: The 4×4 tile under mirror symmetry — paint one quadrant and the kaleidoscope fills the rest. The array meeting the symmetry chapter: reflection is an index map, (n−1−x), and applying it turns a quarter of decisions into a whole of pattern. Economy of authorship, wired into the grid.

pattern_tile_8x8.name: 8x8 Pattern Tile
pattern_tile_8x8.description: Larger 8x8 tile for more complex patterns.
pattern_tile_8x8.qfep_connection: The same puzzle engine as the 4×4 carpet, with tile_size raised to 8 and the symmetry left at SIMPLE: sixty-four authored cells instead of sixteen, so amplification falls exactly as authorship rises. The knob it turns is the ratio between what the hand decides and what the repeat rule multiplies — a bigger source tile is a weaker kaleidoscope.

pattern_tile_brick.name: Brick Pattern Tile
pattern_tile_brick.description: Tile with brick/half-drop offset. Classic masonry pattern.
pattern_tile_brick.qfep_connection: The 4×4 tile with a half-drop offset — masonry's oldest trick, each row shifted so the seams don't line up. The array learning to lie about its own grid: an offset is just index arithmetic, (x + row·k) mod n, and out of that modular shift comes the whole visual strength of a brick wall.

pattern_tile_herringbone.name: Herringbone Pattern Tile
pattern_tile_herringbone.qfep_connection: The tile woven into herringbone — rectangles turned at right angles, the zigzag that floors and fabrics have used for millennia. Pattern as a rule about orientation across indices: the same cell, rotated by its position's parity, and the weave appears from arithmetic no weaver needed to name.

index_visualizer.name: Index Visualizer
index_visualizer.description: Displays current grid position as array index [row, col].
index_visualizer.qfep_connection: A yellow label trails 2.5 m overhead, rounding your continuous stride to [row, col] — you don't read the array, you are its index, discretized live without being asked. The script's own comments argue over which axis counts as the row: even the convention is a treaty, not a fact.

dna.default: craft=pixel - _apply_craft() returns before touching anything, so the scene's baked BoxMesh (0.04 m, albedo 0.8/0.2/0.15, roughness 0.8) and its BoxShape3D are exactly what they were. The 7 existing placements pass no `craft` key, so apply_grid_config sets changed=false and never enters the builder; the puzzle-spawned cubes go through setup()/_create_visual() untouched as before.
dna.was: one plain 4 cm box, the same box whatever colour it carried - the artifact's own truth is 'a pixel is a decision', and it shipped the pixel with no ancestry at all, so every photograph of it was a photograph of a screen unit pretending to be a handmade one
dna.note: NOT one of the six tokens sharing pattern_tile_puzzle.tscn (pattern_tile_puzzle, _4x4, _mirror, _8x8, _brick, _herringbone) - this token has its own scene and its own script, and the .tscn root carries it, so the axis is reachable from a map token. The word is NEW on purpose: the puzzle's own axes (motif, dyelot) are about the pattern and the dye range, not the unit; `unit` is already spent on diamonds for which platonic solid gets stacked, and `facture` carries a fixed cast/facet/armature/shell vocabulary across capsule/folded_strip/triangleprofiles that these values would break. craft asks which trade's hand-held colour unit this is - cut stone, threaded bead, wound spool, moulded brick, or the screen's own lineage-free box. Every value stays inside the 4 cm envelope and the collision shape is never touched, so grab, snap and grid placement are unchanged.

pattern_tile_cube.name: Pattern Tile Cube
pattern_tile_cube.description: Small grabbable color cube for pattern tile puzzle. Drag to grid cells to place colors.
pattern_tile_cube.qfep_connection: The unit you place — a grabbable color cube dragged into a cell of the pattern grid. The atom of the whole chapter made literal: a pattern is built one placed color at a time, and the cube is the single decision the symmetry group will then multiply. Author one; the rule authors the rest.

step_sequencer.name: Step Sequencer
step_sequencer.description: 2D step sequencer with click-to-toggle grid. Arrays as sound - playhead reads indices, triggers sounds.
step_sequencer.qfep_connection: The array played as music: a click-to-toggle grid where a playhead sweeps the indices left to right and triggers sound where it finds a 1. Arrays as time — the same indexed row that held heights now holds beats, and you hear that reading a list in order is exactly what a rhythm is.

step_sequencer_trap.name: Trap Sequencer
step_sequencer_trap.qfep_connection: The signature lives in row three: hi-hats that alternate for half the bar, then collapse into [1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1]. A genre recognizable purely as a change in ones-per-column density — style as subdivision rate.

step_sequencer_synth.name: Synth Sequencer
step_sequencer_synth.description: Synthesizer sequencer with classic synth sounds.
step_sequencer_synth.qfep_connection: TB303, Moog lead, DX7 piano, PPG pad: a pocket history of synthesis loaded onto four tracks. Melody enters the drum machine and finds it indifferent — to the column pointer, a bass note and a kick drum are the same boolean.

step_sequencer_house.name: 90s House Sequencer
step_sequencer_house.description: Crystal Waters / Gypsy Woman style 90s house. TR-909 kick, M1 piano stabs, acid bass.
step_sequencer_house.qfep_connection: The 909 kick, the M1 piano stab, the 303 bass: the Gypsy Woman recipe stored as four track assignments and a 122 BPM constant. Cultural memory shipped as config — swap the dictionary entry and Baltimore becomes Düsseldorf.

step_sequencer_pads.name: Juno Pads Sequencer
step_sequencer_pads.description: Lush analog pads. Juno-106, Jupiter-8, PPG Wave. Slow atmospheric builds.
step_sequencer_pads.qfep_connection: Juno and Jupiter pads at 80 BPM over eight steps push the machine to its own limit: sustain smears across the columns until the grid nearly stops being audible as grid. A test of how much drone a step sequencer can hold before rhythm dissolves into atmosphere.

step_sequencer_kraftwerk.name: Kraftwerk Sequencer
step_sequencer_kraftwerk.description: 1970s Germany. Moog sequencer pulse, robotic precision. The birth of electronic music.
step_sequencer_kraftwerk.qfep_connection: The sequencer plays a sample of the Moog sequencer pulse that taught machines to keep time — origin myth folded into its own config. Robotic precision was never inhuman; it was four Germans in Düsseldorf deciding which cells to set.

step_sequencer_disco.name: Disco Sequencer
step_sequencer_disco.description: 1970s funk and groove. Four-on-floor, Synare disco tom, funky bass.
step_sequencer_disco.qfep_connection: Four-on-the-floor written out literally as [1,0,0,0] four times — the lowest-entropy row in the pattern bank — while the liberation happens in the offbeat hi-hat ones squeezed between the kicks and the Synare tom. The groove is the deviation the anchor makes audible.

step_sequencer_ambient.name: Ambient Works Sequencer
step_sequencer_ambient.description: 1990s Aphex Twin style. Modular textures, drones, ethereal atmosphere.
step_sequencer_ambient.qfep_connection: Eight steps and mostly zeros: the Aphex-style preset teaches that the array's silence is also data. Modular textures and ghost drones hang in what the loop declines to trigger — E_flux carried by the empty cells.

step_sequencer_jazz.name: Jazz Fusion Sequencer
step_sequencer_jazz.description: 1970s Herbie Hancock. Jazz meets electronics, Moog fusion, DX7 piano.
step_sequencer_jazz.qfep_connection: Herbie's Moog fusion and DX7 piano will only ever sound where a boolean says so: improvisation's genre held to a 16-cell schedule. What plays is jazz's residue after quantization — the grid stages exactly what a step machine forecloses.

step_sequencer_chiptune.name: Chiptune Sequencer
step_sequencer_chiptune.description: 1980s 8-bit. C64 SID chip, Amiga tracker, retro game sounds.
step_sequencer_chiptune.qfep_connection: Four sounds salvaged from dead consoles — SID lead, Amiga sample, a jump, a pickup — wired into sixteen steps. The 1980s hardware ceiling replayed as grammar: constraint not as lack but as the compositional engine itself.

step_sequencer_scifi.name: Sci-Fi Lab Sequencer
step_sequencer_scifi.description: Laboratory atmosphere. Hums, data chirps, electromagnetic interference.
step_sequencer_scifi.qfep_connection: No drums at all — lab hum, data chirps, electromagnetic interference, ventilation — sequencing the atmosphere of the laboratory the player is already standing in. The room's ambience unmasked as one more 4×8 boolean schedule.

step_sequencer_cinematic.name: Cinematic Sequencer
step_sequencer_cinematic.description: 1980s Blade Runner. CS-80 brass, Jupiter strings, Vangelis influence.
step_sequencer_cinematic.qfep_connection: Slow the loop to eight steps at 85 BPM, load CS-80 brass and Jupiter strings, and the drum machine scores a film that isn't playing. 'Cinematic' turns out to be a tempo and a timbre assignment, not a different instrument.

step_sequencer_breakbeat.name: Breakbeat Sequencer
step_sequencer_breakbeat.description: 1990s jungle/DnB. Syncopation, chopped samples, fast hi-hats.
step_sequencer_breakbeat.qfep_connection: Jungle enters the matrix as displacement: the same 4×16 booleans as house, but the kicks land off the strong columns and a chopped-sample track does the cutting. Syncopation is the pattern refusing the grid it runs on.

step_sequencer_cosmic.name: Cosmic Sequencer
step_sequencer_cosmic.description: 1970s-80s space disco. Jean-Michel Jarre, ARP 2600, cosmic FX.
step_sequencer_cosmic.qfep_connection: Space is a sound preset: ARP 2600 lead, teleport drone, cosmic FX poured into the ordinary column-by-column traversal. The cosmos here is entirely timbral — underneath, the orbit is the same for-loop as the disco next door.

step_sequencer_lofi.name: Lo-Fi Sequencer
step_sequencer_lofi.description: 2010s chill beats. Warm DX7 piano, mellow 808, study music vibes.
step_sequencer_lofi.qfep_connection: Imperfection as preset: the 'vinyl crackle' is an AMBIENT_WIND sample assigned to track three, synthesized clean and scheduled to the millisecond. Nostalgia for degraded media, manufactured by a machine incapable of wear.

binary_table.name: Binary Table Display
binary_table.description: Show any 2D array as a grid of values. See the data structure made visible.
binary_table.qfep_connection: Digits on a translucent panel, each cell with its address printed in the margin: the confession behind every prettier visualization in the room. Nothing animates — it stages the flat truth that state is values at indices, and everything else is costume.

pulsar_glass_tubes.name: Pulsar Glass Tubes
pulsar_glass_tubes.description: 3D glass tube visualization of Pulsar B1919+21 radio waves. Height = signal intensity. Arrays as art.

pulsar_visualizer.name: Pulsar B1919+21 Visualizer
pulsar_visualizer.description: The first pulsar discovered (1967). Binary table + 3D glass tubes. Joy Division's Unknown Pleasures made interactive.

pulsar_compact.name: Pulsar Compact
pulsar_compact.description: Smaller pulsar visualization. 20 rows of glass tubes.

pulsar_lines.name: Pulsar Lines
pulsar_lines.description: Pulsar visualization using lines instead of tubes. Better performance.

tiling_demo.name: Tiling System Demo
tiling_demo.description: Italian tiling motifs gallery. 17 wallpaper groups, multi-layer composition. Checkerboard to cosmatesque — field study preparation.
tiling_demo.qfep_connection: The gallery of Italian tiling motifs — seventeen wallpaper groups, multi-layer compositions, from plain checkerboard to intricate cosmatesque inlay. The historical proof that this chapter's mathematics is old: the array tiled under symmetry is what medieval floors already were, computed by hand centuries before the grid was a data type.

gallery_marker_facade.name: Gallery Marker — Facade
gallery_marker_facade.description: Bronze pedestal + glowing stake + Label3D reading FACADE. Single-cell sub-gallery anchor used 20+ times across facade maps. Shared scene at commons/artifacts/gallery_marker; the lookup_name fixes the label per gallery_marker_<sequence> alias pattern.
gallery_marker_facade.capacity: POINTS the player at a facades sub-gallery
gallery_marker_facade.qfep_connection: Twenty-odd facade maps share this exact bronze pedestal; only the label FACADE, injected through apply_grid_config, distinguishes it from its PATTERN and other siblings. You-are-here turns out to be a config string, not a geometry.

dna.default: taxonomy=table, chapter=all - both defaults are short-circuits, not recomputations. `table` returns the cell the legacy layout loop already computed, coordinate for coordinate, and every specimen keeps its Label3D at the same offset it always had; `all` admits the array unfiltered in source order, so the loop below sees exactly the array it always saw. All 7 grid placements (Array_Patterns, Corridor_Array_Patterns, Facade_Classical_Orders, Facade_Columns_Rhythm, Facade_Custom_Composition, Facade_Wall_Basics, Facade_Windows_Doors) plus the two curation_station#artifacts collections (Curation_Bay_array_tutorial_1, Curation_Bay_facades_0) pass neither key, and curation_station forwards nothing anyway. The ONE structural change: the twenty specimens and their labels now hang off a `Gallery` Node3D at the origin with an identity transform instead of being parented straight to the root, so a token arriving after _ready can drop them in one call - world positions are unchanged.
dna.was: two exports, `spacing` and `object_height`, both pure dimension, which is why the auto-runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Twenty procedural specimens with their recipes welded into one 240-line function, laid out in a 4x5 lattice with a name label each, and no way for a map to ask the gallery for less than all of it or for a different claim about how the twenty are related.
dna.note: taxonomy is what ORDER the display claims the family has; the members never change. table = the lattice, position IS the recipe's place and every member captioned. ladder = one ascending file, a grammar as a sequence going somewhere. stack = one column on one footprint, twenty descriptions of one object. heap = coordinates abandoned AND the captions withheld, the claim that the classification was ours and the forms never carried it. The captions are the pivot exactly as on the combine benches, and the axis bites hardest here because 'Coral Fingers' and 'Barnacle Sphere' are blue-grey lumps without their labels - the recipe that separates them was never in the picture to begin with. chapter is DERIVED, not written: the source's own row headers already group the twenty four at a time and each header names a class of operation, so _chapter_of reads the grouping off the index rather than restating it in a second list that could fall out of step. topology = the four that only move faces plus the bare seed they are measured against; organic = the four that make a sphere behave like a body; compound = the four where rules act on the OUTPUT of rules, the only place a grammar stops being a filter; decoration = the four that add material the surface did not have; bridge = the L-system and the cellular automaton wired in as operations.
dna.kin: taxonomy and its four values are taken CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER from combine_capsule / combine_sphere / combine_portals, and the ladder/stack/heap placement arithmetic and the _index_hash scatter are theirs unchanged, with object_height added back so the specimens stand on the floor this scene draws and those do not. Same apparatus - a generator's output laid out as a gallery - so it gets the same vocabulary rather than a private one. chapter is deliberately NOT `exhibit` (pattern_mill / pattern_machine_c: bolt|unit|operation|catalogue). That axis asks how much of a CLOSED set of seventeen wallpaper groups the goods put up; this one asks which of five open classes of operation is on the table, and `bolt` means nothing here. Borrowing the word while dropping half its list would claim a comparability that does not exist.
dna.fixture_note: no fixture needed for taxonomy - `heap` scatters from a hash of the index and never randf(), so every boot piles the same pile and the critic measures the axis rather than the noise. NOTE that the SPECIMENS are not all deterministic: several recipes select faces with random:0.12 / up_random and one seeds a cellular automaton at seed_value 42, so the finer forms differ between boots. That noise is common to every value of both axes and pre-dates this promotion; it is paintwork on a large layout change, not a confound, but it is the reason no verdict here should rest on small-percentage differences.
dna.still_note: the scene draws its OWN 14 x 16 floor plane, two DirectionalLight3Ds and a Camera3D, and the floor fills most of any frame. Expect a low subject percentage in every mode and read the bite against the specimens, not the frame. taxonomy separates on gross layout (a 4x5 lattice / a 14 m diagonal file / a 7.8 m column / a 1.3 m pile with no text) and should be unmissable; chapter removes sixteen of twenty objects for any value but `all` and re-centres the remaining four in the same lattice, which is a large change measured against a mostly-empty floor. Both are visible in a single still.
dna.registry_mismatch: FLAGGED, NOT FIXED. This entry's name, description and tags promise an architectural facade gallery with Italian presets - Villa San Michele, Certosa, San Gregorio Armeno - and an element library of columns, arches, cornices and rustication. The scene it points at, res://commons/mesh_grammar/mesh_grammar_demo.tscn, contains none of that: it is a mesh-grammar gallery of twenty organic specimens (coral fingers, petal flowers, barnacle spheres, an L-system tree). Those Italian presets are real and live in commons/facade_parts/presets/ (26 JSON files, including villa_san_michele.json) behind facade_composer_demo.tscn, which no registry token points at. Two maps repeat the false description in their own text (Array_Patterns 'Classical facade presets and elements', Facade_Wall_Basics 'Italian presets showing zoning'). The axes here are DERIVED FROM THE CODE THAT ACTUALLY RUNS, not from the description, which is the only way a declaration can be honest; re-pointing the token or renaming it is a separate decision with 7 placements behind it.

facade_grammar_demo.name: Facade Grammar Demo
facade_grammar_demo.description: Architectural facade gallery. Italian presets (Villa San Michele, Certosa, San Gregorio Armeno) plus element library (columns, arches, cornices, rustication).
facade_grammar_demo.qfep_connection: Architecture as array: Italian facades — Villa San Michele, the Certosa — read as grids of repeating elements, windows and columns indexed across a wall. The chapter's reach into the built world, arguing that a building's rhythm is a data structure, a facade a 2D array of ornament that a grammar fills.

vr_tile_editor.name: VR Tile Editor
vr_tile_editor.description: VR workspace for designing tile patterns. Edit a grid at desk height, see it tile across a floor carpet in real-time. Cycle wallpaper groups with VR controllers.
vr_tile_editor.qfep_connection: The pattern workshop at body scale — edit a tile grid at desk height and watch it tile across the floor around you. The chapter's truth made inhabitable: you design the fundamental domain in your hands and stand inside its repetition, seeing at once that the rule you performed on one tile has performed itself across a room.

vr_tile_editor_mirror.name: VR Tile Editor Mirror
vr_tile_editor_mirror.description: VR tile editor starting in kaleidoscope mirror mode. Design symmetric patterns and see them tile across a floor carpet.
vr_tile_editor_mirror.qfep_connection: The tile editor entered in VR, kaleidoscope mode on — you design a symmetric pattern and watch it tile across a surface around you at body scale. The array's repetition made inhabitable: not a pattern seen on a plate but one you stand inside, the carpet wrapping the room as you paint its seed.

array_carpet.name: Array Carpet
array_carpet.description: A decorative floor carpet displaying the player's tiled pattern from the arrays lesson. Repetition is not boring, it's ornamental.

wfc_tile_mosaic.name: WFC Tile Mosaic
wfc_tile_mosaic.description: Floor panel showing a pre-generated Wave Function Collapse output — a grid of tiles where each cell respects adjacency constraints. Constraint propagation made visible.

dna.fixture_why: Both default to shipped behaviour in code, so neither is an axis. mosaic_seed pins the solve - the shipped seed is hash(global_position + get_instance_id()), and an instance id is different every launch, so five grammar frames would be five different draws and the bite number would measure the RNG. solve_attempts is the shipped max_attempts literal (10) made reachable, and it is here because of the defect below: within 10 attempts a sweep of five values has roughly a 40% chance that at least one tile is not a WFC solve at all but _fallback_grid's two-colour checkerboard. 60 attempts drops that to nil and costs nothing on average, because the loop stops at the first success.
dna.default: grammar=landscape - _grammar_table returns the shipped _adjacency dictionary ITSELF at this value, not a reconstruction of it, so the solver reads the same object, consumes the RNG in the same order and draws the same mosaic. mosaic_seed 0 keeps the shipped position+instance-id hash line character for character and solve_attempts 10 is the literal it replaced. apply_grid_config used to re-seed and re-solve on ANY call and is now guarded twice (a value must validate and differ, and _ready must have generated once) - the only call this artifact receives in the corpus is curation_station's {"emissive": false}, which arrives at the same position and the same instance id _ready saw, so it re-seeded to the identical number and redrew the identical mosaic; removing it changes no pixel in Curation_Bay_mosaicanalysis_1 and saves a whole solve. The other six placements are bare tokens or rotation shorthand and never reach apply_grid_config at all.
dna.was: no declared axis - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. Three exports existed and all three were dimensions: a world size, a grid size and a pixel scale. The artifact's own @identity names its critical parameter as 'the adjacency rules - water may only neighbor water or sand, never stone', and those rules were a literal Dictionary one screen down that no map token could reach. The registry description also called the output 'pre-generated', which is wrong: the WFC is solved live in _ready, every launch.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-04. grammar is the corpus's word for the set of local rules that generates a global form (lsystem_editor, lsystem_architecture, room_grammar) and WFC's adjacency table is exactly that; the values are this system's own laws. They are arranged as a scale of constraint rather than as five flavours: open puts none (and the mosaic falls to salt-and-pepper, which is the artifact's own thesis stated in the negative - the coherence was never the algorithm, it was the rules), landscape is the shipped ecotone, enclave and chain are two different ways of being strict (broker every boundary through ground; or never jump a step in the terrain cycle), and checker is maximal constraint pointing the other way, forbidding a tile its own kind so no region can form at all. All five tables were checked symmetric, and all five were run through a faithful port of this exact solver before being declared.
dna.finding: THE SOLVER HAS A MEASURED DEFECT AND IT IS NOT FIXED HERE. _attempt_solve's entropy scan carries `if min_entropy == 999 and candidates.is_empty(): break` at the row level, which fires the moment ROW 0 is fully collapsed regardless of the other fifteen rows: candidates stays empty, the while loop continues, and the solve spins to max_iterations and reports failure. An attempt therefore only completes when the last cell to collapse happens to lie in row 0. Measured in a faithful port (16x16, one attempt each): landscape completes 31% of attempts, checker 38%, enclave 19%, open 12% - and open constrains NOTHING, which is the proof that the failure is structural and not about the rules. Every failure observed was the iteration cap with 15-22 cells still uncollapsed and ~4880 dead spins burnt; not one was a genuine contradiction. Within the shipped 10-attempt budget that is a ~3% chance of a checkerboard at the default and ~26% under open. Deleting that break is the fix and it is a one-line change to what seven maps draw, so it belongs to a deliberate decision, not to a DNA promotion.
dna.declined: A second axis over the TILE SET (which of the six terrains are in play). It is real and it would be visible, but the alphabet and the rules multiply into invalid pairs - a subset that drops PATH leaves STONE with no legal neighbour under chain, which the solver cannot satisfy and which lands the player on the fallback checkerboard. One axis that always solves beats two that sometimes do not.

pattern_maker_station.name: Pattern Maker Station
pattern_maker_station.description: Interactive wallpaper group station — paint a domain grid on an upright panel, choose from 17 symmetry groups, and watch the tiled result unfold on a large floor carpet in real time.

grid_editor_board.name: Grid Editor Board
grid_editor_board.description: Interactive grid layout editor — Godot VR mirror of the web grid-editor. Control Board subset with 34 elements across 9 categories, 4 presets (Mission Control, Server Rack, Comms Station). Place and arrange control panel components on a 24x14 grid.
grid_editor_board.qfep_connection: A boolean occupancy array is the whole law: elements stamp their footprint, collisions refuse placement, and the upright panel makes visible that layout editing is mostly the management of refusals.

grid_editor_board_3d.name: Grid Editor Board (3D)
grid_editor_board_3d.description: 3D interactive version of the grid editor board. Same layout data as the shadow board but with real 3D elements — CRT monitors with phosphor flicker, VU meters with bouncing needles, interactive push buttons, slider faders, rotary knobs, toggle switches, speakers, and blinking LEDs.
grid_editor_board_3d.qfep_connection: A control panel that is itself a grid map: CRTs, VU meters, and knobs claim cells through the same occupancy logic that lays out rooms, and it accepts the web editor's layouts verbatim. Mission control turns out to be another floor plan — instruments are furniture that claims to be in charge.

grid_3d_capture.name: Grid Editor 3D Capture
grid_3d_capture.description: Procedural 3D builder for all grid editor subsets — chemical models, sticky notes, periodic table, glass racks, big pipes. Accepts subset and preset via config.
grid_3d_capture.qfep_connection: Six subsets share one loader: the identical placement list rises as glassware, a playable synth rack, sticky notes, or a periodic table depending on a single subset string. The grid never learns what it carries — meaning lives entirely in the key, F_order as convention laid over indifferent cells.

facade_builder.name: Facade Builder
facade_builder.description: Interactive architectural facade composer. Five presets (classical, gothic, palazzo, arcade, minimal) with configurable bays, stories, symmetry, and colors. Uses SpatialComposition zones and SurfaceTool geometry.

row_3_x.name: row_3_x
row_3_x.description: Places three pickup cubes in a single row along the X axis.

column_3_z.name: column_3_z
column_3_z.description: Stacks three pickup cubes in the Z direction for spacing tests.

dna.default: notation=label - the pink billboarded [i] built inside the cube loop, the same node in the same place as before, so the 4 existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: a row of four pickup cubes each wearing a pink [i] in the air, which asserted that an index is a tag the object carries and hid that this is one answer among several
dna.note: DERIVED from algorithms/arrays/column_3_z.gd, not composed here - the notation export, the NOTATIONS list and the apply_grid_config handling were already in the script and the registry had never been told, so the sweep could not reach the axis. Count, origin and spacing are identical across all five values; only the notation is dressed on afterwards, inside the row's existing X/Z envelope.

grid_2d_4x4.name: grid_2d_4x4
grid_2d_4x4.description: Builds a 4x4 pickup-cube grid laid out across the floor.

grid_3d_4x4x4.name: grid_3d_4x4x4
grid_3d_4x4x4.description: Populates a 4x4x4 lattice of pickup cubes for volumetric layouts.

grid_snapper.name: grid_snapper
grid_snapper.qfep_connection: Every frame it lerps your actual position toward the nearest integer coordinate — the grid reaching back through the XR origin to discipline the body that walks it. smooth_snap makes the coercion feel like magnetism, which is how discipline prefers to feel.

mondrian_run.name: mondrian_run
mondrian_run.qfep_connection: Mondrian's primaries return as absences: seeded recursive subdivision keeps the black lattice as walkable floor and cuts the red, yellow, and blue out as holes. Composition becomes hazard map — where the painting had colour, the ground has none.

grid_editor_main.name: grid_editor_main
grid_editor_main.qfep_connection: The architect's maquette made an exchange rate: a 12.5 cm cell floated to wrist height commands a one-metre twin snapped to integer world coordinates on the floor. Editing happens at the scale where the hand is strong and lands at the scale where the body must walk — power over space is the coupling between two grids.

IndexVisualizer.name: IndexVisualizer
IndexVisualizer.description: Visualizes current grid index above player
IndexVisualizer.qfep_connection: The floor confesses it was an array all along: round your position, receive an index, wear it overhead as a halo. The script's own comments still argue whether the pair reads [row, col] or [z, x] — the address is certain, the convention never was.

pompeii_mosaic_floor.name: Pompeii Mosaic Floor
pompeii_mosaic_floor.description: Multi-zone Roman mosaic floor from Pompeii. Composes field, border, corner, and threshold patterns using wallpaper group symmetries with opus tessellatum aging effects.

octagon_square_floor.name: Octagon & Square Floor
octagon_square_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with octagon-and-square tessellation — terracotta diamonds inside light octagons with dark interstitial squares.

tumbling_blocks_floor.name: Tumbling Blocks Floor
tumbling_blocks_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with tumbling blocks pattern — three rhombus shades create a 3D cube illusion on a hexagonal grid.

perspective_cubes_floor.name: Perspective Cubes Floor
perspective_cubes_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with perspective cubes pattern — three rhombus shades on a regular rectangular grid create a strong 3D stacked-cube illusion.

diamonds_squares_floor.name: Diamonds in Squares Floor
diamonds_squares_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with diamonds-in-squares pattern. Each cell contains a 45-degree rotated diamond inscribed in a square, alternating dark/light in a checkerboard arrangement.

nested_diamonds_floor.name: Nested Diamonds Floor
nested_diamonds_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with nested diamonds pattern. Each cell contains three concentric 45-degree rotated squares creating a bulls-eye of dark-light-dark-light zones radiating inward.

swastika_meander_floor.name: Swastika Meander Floor
swastika_meander_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with swastika meander (Greek key labyrinth) pattern. Continuous dark meander path on light background with terracotta accent squares at cell centers.

solomons_knot_floor.name: Solomon's Knot Floor
solomons_knot_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with Solomon's Knot (nodo di Salomone) — two interlocked loops forming an infinite knot, a classic Roman/Byzantine decorative motif with over-under weave in three colors.

stepped_zigzag_floor.name: Stepped Zigzag Floor
stepped_zigzag_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with stepped zigzag pattern — interlocking L-shaped steps in three tones create a 3D staircase illusion reminiscent of Escher's impossible staircases.

flower_of_life_floor.name: Flower of Life Floor
flower_of_life_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with Flower of Life sacred geometry pattern — overlapping circles on a hexagonal grid creating petal shapes at intersections. Dark circle outlines on light background with terracotta accent petals.

polka_dot_field_floor.name: Polka Dot Field Floor
polka_dot_field_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with dark field and scattered small light tesserae in a regular grid with organic jitter. Common in vestibules and corridors, bordered by a meander pattern.

meander_threshold_floor.name: Meander Threshold Floor
meander_threshold_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic threshold floor with bold Greek key meander border framing a dark field with scattered white tesserae. Common Roman doorway pattern placed at transitions between rooms.

pompeii_meander_floor.name: Pompeii Meander Floor
pompeii_meander_floor.description: Greek key meander border drawn as actual geometry — thick rectangular quads for each line segment rather than bitmap pixels. Crisp, thick, properly proportioned meander lines at any scale with dark polka-dot interior field.

exact_meander_floor.name: Exact Meander Floor
exact_meander_floor.description: Faithful pixel reproduction of a Pompeii meander floor from photograph. 84x66 grid with continuous Greek key meander border (3-cell dark lines on light band, 12-cell border depth), L-bend corners, and dark field with scattered white tesserae.

double_snake_meander.name: Double Snake Meander
double_snake_meander.description: Greek key meander generated by TWO mirrored self-avoiding walks that dance around each other. Snake A hugs the outer edge, Snake B hugs the inner edge. Their interlocking territories produce the classic meander pattern. Dark field interior with polka dots.

free_meander_floor.name: Free Meander Floor
free_meander_floor.description: Rule-based Greek key meander — no tiles, no turtle, no bitmap. Each cell decides its own color from ONE modular arithmetic rule applied to its global position. The entire pattern is: territory = ((pos_along + ring * band_width) % period) < half_period. Dark field interior with polka dots.

mirror_snake_meander.name: Mirror Snake Meander
mirror_snake_meander.description: Greek key meander via mirrored self-avoiding crossing snakes. Solve one quarter of the border, mirror X to complete each side, mirror Y to create the interlocking counter-snake. The crossings emerge automatically from the mirroring. Four depth bands where bands 0/3 and 1/2 are mirrors produce the classic Pompeii hook pattern.

braid_meander_floor.name: Braid Meander Floor
braid_meander_floor.description: Greek key meander generated TOP-DOWN from braid topology. Two strands cross at regular intervals; each crossing projects onto the grid as an angular spiral hook. The braid crossing number controls the pattern: 1 = classic Greek key, 2 = double meander. Dark field interior with polka dots.

star_rosette_floor.name: Star Rosette Floor
star_rosette_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with hexagonal star rosette (hexagram) pattern. Six-pointed stars formed by overlapping equilateral triangles with small rhombi between stars. Classic Roman geometric mosaic.

floor_plan_space.name: Floor Plan Space
floor_plan_space.description: Standalone 3D space builder that loads a floor_plan.json and constructs rooms with facade walls and mosaic floors, independent of the grid system. DNA: solidity decides whether the plan is a drawing you pass through (diagram) or a building that stops you (built — walls get colliders and the JSON's doorways become the only openings); bay_span is the facade module in metres, the rhythm of columns and openings on every wall. Token: floor_plan_space#solidity:built#bay_span:4.5.

dna.default: solidity=diagram, bay_span=3.0 - diagram is the commented-out collider block left off, and 3.0 is the literal in roundi(width / 3.0), so all 23 existing placements build byte-identical geometry
dna.was: no declared axes at all. The wall colliders existed as a commented-out block marked 'players can walk through walls for now', and the facade bay module was the bare literal 3.0 - so an artifact that claims a floor plan becomes an inhabitable space shipped a space no body could touch
dna.note: The artifact's truth statement is that a room is a grammar of connections, not a boundary. Under solidity=diagram the doorways in the JSON are decoration - you walk through the walls too. Under built they are the argument.

radial_mandala_floor.name: Radial Mandala Floor
radial_mandala_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with concentric radial mandala pattern. A terracotta 6-pointed star rosette at center, surrounded by rings of alternating dark/light triangles radiating outward with interlocking offset.

guilloche_border_floor.name: Guilloche Border Floor
guilloche_border_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with prominent guilloche (braided rope) border surrounding a simple checkerboard grid field with a central terracotta pictorial panel inset. The guilloche band features interlocking S-curves in dark, light and terracotta tesserae.

honeycomb_hex_floor.name: Honeycomb Hex Floor
honeycomb_hex_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with honeycomb hexagonal tessellation. Regular hexagons in alternating dark/light with dark grout outlines. Every 3rd hexagon features a small terracotta cross motif at its center.

diamond_lattice_floor.name: Diamond Lattice Floor
diamond_lattice_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with diamond lattice pattern. Two sets of diagonal lines at 45 and 135 degrees cross to form a regular rhombus grid. Alternating dark/light diamonds create a rotated checkerboard effect.

multi_zone_carpet_floor.name: Multi-Zone Carpet Floor
multi_zone_carpet_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor demonstrating carpet composition — nested rectangular bands of distinct motifs (dark border, sawtooth chevrons, scallop semicircles) surrounding a central checkerboard field. Demonstrates the Roman principle of hierarchical spatial framing.

wave_scale_floor.name: Wave Scale Floor
wave_scale_floor.description: Roman imbrication (fish-scale) mosaic floor — overlapping semicircles arranged in offset rows creating a wave/scale effect. Common in Roman baths and fountains. Alternating dark, light, and terracotta rows with grout arc outlines.

pelta_shield_floor.name: Pelta Shield Floor
pelta_shield_floor.description: Roman pelta (Amazon shield) mosaic floor — interlocking crescent shapes with concave bites arranged in offset rows. A classic Roman border and field pattern where paired crescents face opposite directions, creating a rhythmic shield motif.

basket_weave_floor.name: Basket Weave Floor
basket_weave_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with basket weave (opus spicatum) pattern. Alternating horizontal and vertical pairs of 2:1 rectangular tiles in a checkerboard arrangement create a woven textile appearance. Dark and light pairs interlock like fabric.

herringbone_floor.name: Herringbone Floor
herringbone_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with herringbone (opus spicatum) pattern. Rectangular 2:1 bricks laid at 45-degree angles in alternating zigzag rows. Adjacent bricks point in opposite directions creating the classic V/chevron pattern found in Roman and medieval floors.

labyrinth_floor.name: Labyrinth Floor
labyrinth_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with classical 7-circuit labyrinth pattern. A single unbroken path spirals inward from the entrance to the center — not a maze but a meditation in stone. Based on Roman house labyrinths found across the Mediterranean.

san_michele_mosaic_floor.name: San Michele Mosaic Floor
san_michele_mosaic_floor.description: Circular Roman mosaic floor inspired by Villa San Michele, Capri. Concentric zones read from outside in: circular vine scroll border, square Greek key meander frame, dark solid band, classical 7-circuit labyrinth, and a central terracotta rosette.

tile_meander_floor.name: Tile Meander Floor
tile_meander_floor.description: Greek key meander floor built from exactly 3 tile types: field (solid blue), straight (horizontal key hook), and corner (90-degree turn). Villa San Michele blue majolica style. Each tile is a 7x7 bitmap; when tiled along all 4 borders, they form a continuous Greek key band.

dense_carpet_floor.name: Dense Carpet Floor
dense_carpet_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor imitating woven textile: a dark field covered in hundreds of tiny light crosses arranged in a dense offset grid, creating a carpet/tweed effect.

opus_sectile_floor.name: Opus Sectile Floor
opus_sectile_floor.description: Opus sectile marble floor � large cut stone pieces forming bold geometric patterns. Grid of circles inscribed in squares with triangular corner fills in 4+ marble colors (basalt, terracotta, serpentine green, porphyry red). Cosmatesque / Pantheon style.

spiral_mosaic_floor.name: Spiral Mosaic Floor
spiral_mosaic_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with Archimedean spiral pattern. A single continuous dark spiral band winds from a central rosette outward on a light background, widening as it goes. Ancient symbol found across cultures from Newgrange to Roman mosaics.

interlocking_t_floor.name: Interlocking T Floor
interlocking_t_floor.description: Procedural Pompeii mosaic floor with interlocking T-shaped tetromino pattern. T-pieces (3 wide x 2 tall) tile with alternating rotations and colors, dark Ts pointing down interlock with light Ts pointing up, creating a satisfying puzzle-like woven surface.

compass_rose_floor.name: Compass Rose Floor
compass_rose_floor.description: Procedural compass rose mosaic floor � 16-pointed mariner's star with alternating dark/light triangular wedges radiating from a terracotta center disc. Inner ring of 8 narrow intercardinal points, outer ring of 8 cardinal points, surrounded by concentric border bands.

windmill_floor.name: Windmill Floor
windmill_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with windmill/pinwheel pattern. Each unit has a small terracotta center square surrounded by 4 L-shaped blades — two dark, two light opposite — creating a spinning windmill effect. Adjacent units rotate 90 degrees for continuous flow.

chain_link_floor.name: Chain Link Floor
chain_link_floor.description: Pompeii mosaic floor with interlocking circles arranged so each passes through its neighbors centers, creating a continuous chain. Classic Roman guilloche derivative. Overlapping areas form pointed vesica piscis shapes filled in terracotta.

pixel_invader_floor.name: Pixel Invader Floor
pixel_invader_floor.description: Procedural pixel art floor with space invader sprites tiled in electric green on a black field. 11x8 bitmap characters march across the ground like an 8-bit arcade screen.

neon_chevron_floor.name: Neon Chevron Floor
neon_chevron_floor.description: Procedural pixel art floor with bold V-shaped chevron stripes radiating from center. Hot pink, electric blue, yellow, and purple bands alternate with black gaps for a rainbow V pattern.

glitch_grid_floor.name: Glitch Grid Floor
glitch_grid_floor.description: Procedural pixel art floor with digital noise aesthetic. Mostly black grid with ~18% of cells lit in hot pink, cyan, lime, red, or white using deterministic hash for reproducible glitch pattern.

memphis_floor.name: Memphis Pattern Floor
memphis_floor.description: Procedural pixel art floor inspired by Memphis Group / Sottsass design. Pastel pink background with scattered black triangles, yellow dots, and teal zigzag shapes placed by pseudo-random hash.

rainbow_checker_floor.name: Rainbow Checkerboard Floor
rainbow_checker_floor.description: Procedural pixel art floor with rainbow checkerboard pattern. Each row uses a different spectrum color paired with black: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple — then repeats.

pixel_cross_floor.name: Pixel Cross Carpet Floor
pixel_cross_floor.description: Procedural pixel art floor with large 5x5 pixel crosses on a dark background. Alternating bright green and hot pink crosses in staggered rows create a bold carpet effect.

turtle_meander_floor.name: Turtle Meander Floor
turtle_meander_floor.description: Procedural mosaic floor whose Greek key border is traced by a turtle graphics engine. The same turtle machine generates the ancient meander, the Hilbert curve, and the Peano curve — different programs, same machine.

space_filling_floor.name: Space-Filling Floor
space_filling_floor.description: Procedural mosaic floor demonstrating the connection between ancient meanders and modern space-filling curves. Four modes — Greek key, Hilbert, Peano, Penrose — each answer: how do you fill a bounded area with a path?

grid_model.name: Grid Model
grid_model.description: Miniature interactive model of the map grid — grab cubes to reshape terrain. Teaches layout_data[z][x] = height as a physical 2D array.

pattern_tile_plate.name: Pattern Tile Plate
pattern_tile_plate.description: Dieter Rams-styled pattern studio. Paint a 4x4 grid, see it tile into a carpet using 17 wallpaper symmetry groups. Integrated cream plate with palette, preview, and symmetry controls.
pattern_tile_plate.qfep_connection: A Dieter Rams-styled studio: paint a 4×4 grid, see it tile through the seventeen wallpaper symmetries into a carpet. The chapter's most complete pattern instrument — the array's repetition crossed with the plane's exactly seventeen ways of repeating, design reduced to choosing a tile and a group.

pattern_studio_plate.name: Pattern Studio Plate
pattern_studio_plate.description: Full pattern design studio ported from Three.js PatternMaker3D. Cream plate with 4x4 paint grid, 3x3 palette, 6 sliders (motif, group, period, size, zone, site), control buttons, and real-time carpet output using all 17 wallpaper symmetry groups. 10 Italian motifs and 5 historical period palettes.
pattern_studio_plate.qfep_connection: The full pattern studio, ported from PatternMaker3D — a cream plate with paint grids and symmetry controls, the array-as-pattern given a proper workbench. Where the single tiles teach one move each, this gathers them: paint, symmetrize, tile, all in one hand, the chapter's craft consolidated.

sorting_algorithm_race.name: Sorting Algorithm Race
sorting_algorithm_race.description: Four rows of 16 colored bars sort simultaneously using Bubble, Insertion, Selection, and Merge sort. Animated step-by-step so you can watch algorithms race and feel the difference in strategy.

lattice_walk.description: The array seam. An array is a lattice - integer addresses, no cells between. The amber line is the continuous path you want across the grid; the blue staircase is the path you can occupy: whole cells, the line rounded to the nearest lattice point. Reach for element 2.5 and you snap to 2 or 3. The smooth intention survives only as a stair of held cells.
lattice_walk.name: Lattice Walk
lattice_walk.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for array_tutorial. Bias is conserved; show the seam.

gallery_marker_pattern.name: Gallery Marker — Pattern
gallery_marker_pattern.description: Bronze pedestal + glowing stake + Label3D reading PATTERN. Single-cell sub-gallery anchor for the Pattern_pt01..pt10 wallpaper-group maps. Shared scene at commons/artifacts/gallery_marker; the lookup_name fixes the label per gallery_marker_<sequence> alias pattern.
gallery_marker_pattern.qfep_connection: The stake anchoring ten wallpaper-group rooms holds no pattern itself: the same shared gallery_marker scene as every other sequence, with PATTERN written in by config. The symmetry groups get a signpost whose only symmetry-breaking is a word.

dna.default: mode=stake - the shipped code path, so existing placements are unchanged
dna.was: the gallery_marker family shares request_note's attachment axis: how a sign meets the world it points at. It was billboarding in mid-air
dna.note: declared by hand 2026-07-29 — the axis was already in the script and the registry had never been told, so the sweep could not reach it
